name: SplashCursor-TS-TW
title: Fluid Splash Cursor
description: Liquid dye in green, violet and amber blooms under the pointer and streams across a black panel, curling and dissolving like ink in water.
use: A bold brand page wants a full-screen fluid playground behind its content.
avoid: It adds a fixed full-screen canvas and runs a heavy simulation every frame, which can overwhelm text.
a11y: Decorative and pointer-driven, with a non-stop simulation that ignores reduced-motion preferences. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A black panel with a faint letterspaced hint. The pointer leaves soft clouds of green, magenta and amber smoke, bright at the centre and feathering away into black.
behaves: Moving or dragging the mouse injects dye and velocity into a fluid simulation, so blobs curl into ribbons and slowly dissolve. Releasing stops new dye while the existing colour fades out.
customise: Simulation and dye resolution, dissipation, pressure, curl, splat radius and force, shading, background, transparency, rainbow mode and colour are props.
weight: heavy: A multi-pass fluid simulation runs curl, vorticity, pressure and advection passes every frame.
demo: Faint hint "Move or drag your cursor anywhere".
issues: The demo text is nearly invisible against the black and gets covered by dye.
The fixed canvas spans the whole viewport, so it can tint or block other page content.
polishWhy: Ribbons of dye look genuinely fluid and the colours mix well; the page copy is lost in the dark.
